messages:
mia: FYI I opened a docs PR that consolidates the Dedicated capacity autoscale examples and adds an FAQ section for the 'soft-eviction' behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123

alex: thanks, looking now. main things to check: terraform snippet, python sdk example, and the SLA wording.

sophia: can you call out the migration steps for customers moving from reserved pools? we want a short checklist + a note about metric drift after migration.

mia: yep added a short migration checklist under /docs/dedicated/migration.md. it’s intentionally terse — 4 steps. asking for wording check on step 2 (drain vs cordon).

raul: quick read. step 2: we should prefer `cordon` in the docs for safety, then `drain` only when you can tolerate in-flight evictions. reworded suggestion in the PR comment.

jen: tiny nit: the SLA table currently says "SLA: 99.9%" in one place and "99.95%" in another — which is correct for Dedicated? that mismatch will confuse sales.

mia: Dedicated SLA is 99.95% for standard reserved capacity. I updated the table but missed one reference — fixing that now.

alex: the python SDK snippet uses `client.dedicated.provision(...)` but our SDK recently changed method name to `client.capacity.create_dedicated(...)`. can we update the snippet before merge?

sophia: also the terraform sample uses an old annotation `redwood.dedicated/isolate=true`. we standardized annotations last quarter to `redwood.capacity/isolation=dedicated`. please update.

mia: good catches. updating both snippets. new terraform example in the PR now:` ``hcl
resource \"redwood_dedicated_pool\" \"example\" {
  name = \"analytics-dedicated\"
  gpu  = \"a100\"
  annotations = {
    \"redwood.capacity/isolation\" = \"dedicated\"
  }
  autoscale_policy = \"balanced\"
}
` ``

raul: looks clearer. one more: we should include a tiny note about the interaction between autoscale `min_replicas` and our soft-eviction policy. people got tripped up when min_replicas=0 + eviction window is small.

mia: added an FAQ entry: "Why did my pool evict despite min_replicas=0?" short answer and link to an internal explainer.

alex: SDK example updated?

mia: updated to the new Python call, example:` ``python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.capacity.create_dedicated(name=\"analytics-dedicated\", gpu_type=\"a100\", autoscale={\"policy\":\"balanced\"})
print(resp.id)
` ``

jen: small wording suggestion: replace "evict" with "preempt" in FAQ to align with product glossary.

sophia: agree. also add a short sentence about expected metric stabilization time (48 hours) after migration. customers keep asking that.

mia: done. added that sentence and referenced the rollout checklist.

alex: can someone sanity-check the links? one of the link fixes from last sprint apparently regressed and 3 internal links are 404.

raul: I validated two links. third one points to the old runbook path — changed to /runbooks/dedicated-eviction. updated in the PR.

jen: LGTM from docs ops, left a few style nits inline.

sophia: left a note to add a tiny diagram (png) that explains isolation levels (shared vs reserved vs dedicated). we have an asset in Figma — but need the exported PNG. @design-team can you export 800x400 and drop in assets/imgs?

mia: pinging design separately. for now added a placeholder image and alt text.

alex: CI (docsite build) is flaky today but try re-run.

deploy-bot: docsite build started for PR #4123

deploy-bot: docsite build passed — preview: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/pr-4123/ (auto-deployed) :tada:

mia: thanks all. plan: merge after design png is added or we can ship with placeholder and iterate. if no objections I'll merge tomorrow noon PST.

jen: ship it with placeholder, add a follow-up task to replace png.

sophia: +1 ship it. i'll open a follow-up PR for the diagram once design uploads.

raul: +1. one reminder — update the changelog entry so PMs can call out the migration doc in the release notes.

mia: added changelog note. merging now. thanks everyone!
